title: Simultaneous parameters for a clean regular pair and a regular subflag
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $P,Q,K\subsetneq R$ be ideals with $P+Q\subseteq K$, and assume that $R/P$, $R/Q$, $R/(P+Q)$ and $R/K$ are regular local. There is a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], an integer $0\le l\le d$, and subsets $A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,l\}$ such that $K=(t_1,\ldots,t_l)$, $P=(t_a:a\in A)$ and $Q=(t_b:b\in B)$. Zero ideals, $P=Q$, $K=P+Q$, and dimension zero are allowed.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120, with extension of the parameters in the regular quotient by P+Q to accommodate the regular subscheme defined by K; used in Proposition 4.2.8(iii), printed p.121.

proof.text: Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$, $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, $S=P+Q$, and $U_L=(L+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2\subseteq V$ for $L=P,Q,S,K$. All these ideals lie in $\mathfrak m$ since $S\subseteq K\subsetneq R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $V$ has finite dimension $d=\dim R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators] to each $L$: it has generators $g_i$ with independent classes in $V$. Consequently $L\cap\mathfrak m^2=\mathfrak mL$: if $x=\sum a_i g_i$ has zero class in $V$, independence gives $a_i\in\mathfrak m$ for all $i$, and the reverse inclusion follows from $L\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Thus the natural map $L/\mathfrak mL\to U_L$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00NR, lemma-regular-quotient-regular, proof; cotangent dimension discussion before Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local; also ILO VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: Every $w\in U_P\cap U_Q$ has a representative in $P\cap Q$. Indeed choose $p\in P$, $q\in Q$ representing $w$. Then $p-q\in S\cap\mathfrak m^2=\mathfrak mS=\mathfrak mP+\mathfrak mQ$ by step 1 and distributivity of ideal multiplication. Write $p-q=u+v$ with $u\in\mathfrak mP$, $v\in\mathfrak mQ$. The element $c=p-u=q+v$ lies in $P\cap Q$ and still represents $w$, since $u,v\in\mathfrak m^2$. This explicitly supplies the common lifts needed below.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120, last paragraph: the reduction of the intersection-sum exact sequence modulo the maximal ideal; written here directly using step 1.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] applied to the vector space $U_P\cap U_Q$, choose a basis $C$ of that intersection. Use step 2 to lift its members to elements $c_i\in P\cap Q$. Apply the same basis-extension statement in $U_P$ and $U_Q$ to obtain bases $C\sqcup X$ of $U_P$ and $C\sqcup Y$ of $U_Q$, and lift $X$ to elements $x_i\in P$ and $Y$ to elements $y_i\in Q$. The family $C\sqcup X\sqcup Y$ is a basis of $U_P+U_Q=U_S$. For independence, a relation makes the $X$-combination lie in $U_P\cap U_Q=\operatorname{span}_k C$; independence of $C\sqcup X$ kills its $X$ coefficients. Independence of $C\sqcup Y$ kills the remaining coefficients. Spanning follows by adding the two displayed spans.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120: independent cotangent directions for the transverse pair, after lifting the common directions; the common directions are handled together rather than by successive quotients.

proof.text: As $U_S\subseteq U_K\subseteq V$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] first in $U_K$ to extend $C\sqcup X\sqcup Y$ to a basis $C\sqcup X\sqcup Y\sqcup Z$, and then in $V$ to extend that basis by $T$. Lift $Z$ to elements $z_i\in K$, and lift $T$ to elements $v_i\in\mathfrak m$. Retain the already chosen lifts of $C,X,Y$. These families are finite because $V$ is finite dimensional. Let $t$ be their concatenation in the order $(c_i),(x_i),(y_i),(z_i),(v_i)$, and let $l$ be the total length of the first four blocks. Its classes are a basis of $V$, and the first $l$ classes are a basis of $U_K$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120, completion of cotangent directions to parameters; extension through the intermediate subspace for K in the setting of Proposition 4.2.8(iii), printed p.121.

proof.text: Use the isomorphisms of step 1: the chosen $c_i,x_i$ span $P/\mathfrak mP$, the $c_i,y_i$ span $Q/\mathfrak mQ$, and the first $l$ entries of $t$ span $K/\mathfrak mK$. These are finite $R$-modules since $R$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to each ideal as an $R$-module. It gives $P=(c_i,x_i)$, $Q=(c_i,y_i)$, and $K=(t_1,\ldots,t_l)$. Apply that same statement to the finite module $\mathfrak m$ and the full cotangent basis: $(t)=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK, local generation form, applied to the four finite modules P, Q, K and the maximal ideal.

proof.text: The list $t$ has length $d$, because its classes form a basis of the $d$-dimensional space $V$. Together with $(t)=\mathfrak m$, this is exactly a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Take $A$ to be the positions of the $c_i,x_i$ blocks and $B$ the positions of the $c_i,y_i$ blocks. Both are subsets of $\{1,\ldots,l\}$, and step 5 gives all three required ideal equalities. Empty blocks are permitted throughout, so no step excludes $P=0$, $Q=0$, $P=Q$, $K=S$, or $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local; the regular-parameter definition and the final ordering of the constructed basis.

proof_origin.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.6, printed p.120: the intersection-sum cotangent argument, reorganized into simultaneous bases; the regular subflag is incorporated by an extra basis extension through the image of K. Stacks Tags 00NR and 00DV supply the algebraic inputs.
